payload.title: welcome banner shows the correct signed-in user's name
payload.errorMessage:
expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed

Locator: getByTestId('welcome-banner')
Expected: "Welcome, Priya"
Received: "Welcome, Alex"

note: A wrong username in a welcome banner reads like a serious session-mixup bug, not a flake — and this run recorded a single failure with no retry to disprove it. But an intermittent 5-in-45 historical rate on this exact assertion — never zero, never spiking — is the wrong shape for a deterministic session-mixup bug, which would fail every time a stale session exists, not occasionally. That pattern matches a client-side session-cache read racing the fresh-login response — the previous test worker's cached user object is read once before the new session settles, then self-corrects on its own timeline rather than on retry. A one-shot read alone would call this REAL_BUG and could trigger a false security-adjacent alarm.
